$comment: Every number and label SYNAPSE shows must trace back to an id in this file, or be marked as an assumption. docs/sources.md is generated from it (make sources).

challenge.title: Space Apps 2026 challenge: Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions
findings: Asks for a visual tool so astronauts can assess their health indicators and get guidance
Accepts keyboard, mouse or camera input

hrp-hazards.title: NASA HRP: 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight
findings: Five hazards: Space Radiation; Isolation and Confinement; Distance from Earth; Gravity Fields; Hostile/Closed Environments
On Mars, astronauts would live in 3/8 of Earth's gravity for up to two years; a Mars trip lasts about three years
Hostile/Closed Environments covers habitability: temperature, pressure, lighting, noise, microbes, immune responses
No numeric thresholds

hrp-risks.title: NASA HRP: Risks of Human Spaceflight
findings: 17 official risks in three groups: human physiology, behavioral performance and human factors, space radiation
None of them is about cabin CO2
No numeric thresholds

hrp-ongoing-research.title: NASA HRP: Ongoing HRP Research
findings: ARCHeR tracked the Artemis II crew's wellbeing, activity and sleep with a wrist actigraphy device (as summarized in the plan)

csa-radiation.title: CSA: Monitoring radiation for astronaut health (2026-02-26)
findings: CANS is a compact, autonomous instrument to measure neutron radiation exposure in space
Neutron radiation contributes about 30% of total radiation on the ISS
No dose dataset

csa-why-science.title: CSA: Why do we conduct science experiments in space?
findings: Context for the Science Contribution Score and the Earth-use closing of the pitch

jones-2022-sleep.title: Jones et al. (2022), Sleep deficiency in spaceflight is associated with degraded neurobehavioral functions and elevated stress in astronauts on six-month missions aboard the ISS, Sleep
findings: 24 astronauts on 6-month ISS missions, Reaction Self Test with PVT-B
Astronauts reported sleeping 6.5 h on average in flight
Sleep under 6 h was associated with slower psychomotor response, higher stress and workload
Sleep under 5 h was associated with negative somatic states
Sleep was self-reported

flynn-evans-2016-circadian.title: Flynn-Evans et al. (2016), Circadian misalignment affects sleep and medication use before and during spaceflight, npj Microgravity
findings: Actigraphy from 21 ISS missions, 3,248 days of spaceflight
Sleep averaged 6.4 h when aligned with circadian timing and 5.4 h when misaligned

basner-2011-pvtb.title: Basner, Mollicone & Dinges (2011), Validity and sensitivity of a brief psychomotor vigilance test (PVT-B) to total and partial sleep deprivation, Acta Astronautica
findings: 3-minute PVT-B
Lapse threshold lowered from 500 ms to 355 ms
Inter-stimulus interval 1-4 s per the paper (secondary sources differ: check the original)

nasa-pvt-iss.title: Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT) on ISS (data.nasa.gov)
findings: Design reference for the PVT-B; link may have changed

nasa-standard-measures.title: NASA Spaceflight Standard Measures (NTRS)
findings: Raw per-astronaut data is not public; HRP shares it only through data sharing agreements

asrs-report-sets.title: NASA ASRS Database Report Sets
findings: Aviation incident narratives, including crew fatigue sets
Source for the forensic intro script

uta-rldd.title: UTA Real-Life Drowsiness Dataset
findings: About 30 h of webcam/phone video from 60 people: alert, low vigilance, drowsy
Main training set for the fatigue model
Paper: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.07312

drozy.title: DROZY drowsiness database (University of Liege)
findings: 14 subjects, 28-30 h awake; face video, polysomnography, KSS and PVT synchronized

yawdd.title: YawDD yawning detection dataset
findings: Videos of drivers talking, singing and yawning; validates yawn detection

mrl-eye.title: MRL Eye Dataset
findings: 84,898 infrared eye images, open or closed; optional check of the eye-closed threshold
